Adding the initial sizing notes below (high-level — we should run an actual perf spike to validate):

- Assumptions: average query = 1.2k tokens, 95th pct latency target = 250ms for generation, embeddings requests batched separately with throughput target 20k emb/sec sustained for initial ingest window.

- Dedicated sizing recommendation (starter commit): 4 x A100-class GPUs with autoscale up to 12 for expected peak. Min pool = 2 GPUs for redundancy.

- Autoscale thresholds: scale-up when queue depth > 25 requests for 30s OR p95 CPU/GPU utilization > 78% for 60s. Scale-down after 5m of sustained utilization < 35% with gradual ramp to avoid flapping.

- Concurrency limits: per-GPU token-concurrency modeled as (GPU_tokens_per_second * target_latency_budget) / avg_query_tokens. Practically, set model_concurrency=8 for generation and 32 for embeddings workers initially.

- Queue strategy: prioritize interactive generation traffic over bulk embedding ingestion. Use separate logical queues with separate autoscale signals; embedding queue can run batch-only workers that accept backfilled jobs.

- Reranker placement: colocate reranker on the same Dedicated pool if your p95 search latency requirement is < 150ms; otherwise run reranker on a separate pool optimized for short-context models.

Attachments: throughput-estimates.csv (simple table with qps -> GPU counts).
